recipe.notes:
Served = the client renders the template (the query prompt for queries, bare text for documents) and POSTs strings to /v1/embeddings; vLLM v0.33.0 serves the checkpoint with --runner pooling only (pooling and normalisation resolve from the checkpoint's own sentence-transformers metadata; no --hf-overrides, no chat template, no trust_remote_code, no plugin). Prompt format: the frame ends with "Query:" and the query follows with NO space; the card's own TEI curl example writes a space after "Query:" and shifts the ids (measured divergence at index 19) -- the sentence-transformers prompts and the card's Python snippets are the canonical no-space form. Instruction: the query frame IS the instruction (config_sentence_transformers.json prompts.query); specialising the task means rewriting the frame in this recipe (a new content identity), never a per-run or server-side instruction field. Anchor: the served route appends the tokenizer's post-processor endoftext (id 151643) and last-token pooling reads it -- the query shape ends on its content span and pins add_special_tokens: true, declaring that appended token as the shape's anchor (the harness's anchor audit reads the post-processor's tail alone there; the product refuses an empty fixed segment, and this content-final declaration is what it offers instead). Truncation: client.max_tokens is 8192 (the card's example budget); the cut applies to the query span only, after reserving the frame (19 content ids + the appended anchor: overhead 20 and 1 for query and document, measured) and re-attaching the frame, so the anchor always survives -- the card's own HF truncation keeps the same invariant (8191 content+frame ids + the anchor at 8192, measured at 9008 tokens), while a naive first-8192-token cut of the rendered ids drops it and diverges at exactly the pooled token (measured). The card cuts ids while the client cuts verbatim text, so over the cap the content boundary can differ while both keep the anchor: the recipe declares over_cap_cut_differs, the reference's render is the card's uncut prompt (it never ports the client's cut), over-cap rows ride the harness's non-gating table and under-cap rows gate byte-exactly. Wiring: every request is fitted to the declared budget on the wire by the merged product's embedding client (rcp.data.preprocess.fit), audited in stage 1 against the captured wire. Per-shape query caps (whether query_max_tokens applies): no separate query cap exists in the referent -- the card's transformers path truncates queries and documents alike at 8192 -- so query_max_tokens is not declared and both shapes draw on max_tokens. The engine image's transformers pin at the tag is >=5.16.1, <5.21.0 (requirements/common.txt); the tokenizer files are pinned by revision and the stage-1 zero-tolerance token-id check on the GPU host is the designed catch for library drift. No media processor settings (mm_processor_kwargs) apply: the model is text-only (input: [text], no processor files in the repo). Reference environment: reference.in/reference.lock (torch, transformers; render mode needs only huggingface_hub -- see reference.py). Precision bounds (stage 2; the rc4 wave and the same corpus's E2 r3 run): the served engine and the reference both run bf16 (config.json torch_dtype; the reference loads it unchanged), so the residual is the two bf16 kernel stacks (vLLM's attention/pooling against the card's HF path), not a dtype cast. The rc4 wave (69 vectors, 207 comparisons at full width, k=32 and k=1024) measured the 0.6b at 0.9992973389 full width (was 0.9990227618 at E2 r3, the 5.19-era transformers) and 0.9988384352 at k=32 (was 0.9989077419); the same vectors both eras, so the movement is the bf16 stacks' rounding, and the full width improved. The k=32 minimum is a STABLE low row, not a one-off: row 14 query was 0.9989372 (second worst) at E2 r3 and moved -9.87e-5, while E2 r3's worst (row 15 query) recovered +3.97e-4. The corpus's largest per-vector movement at k=32 between the two eras is 3.974e-4, so the family's `gates.vec_min_cosine` is 0.9988384352 - 3.974e-4 = 0.9984410, declared 0.9984 (rounded down): the engine's own noise can land its worst observed move on the min row without a false red, and a real regression (a cast, a wrong pooled token, the media-approximation class at 1e-3) still fails. The 0.6b inherits it (its overrides.gates carries no bound). The one scalar also gates the full width, where 0.9992973389 leaves 9.0e-4 of headroom, so that gate stays a gate; a per-MRL-dim floor (the full width at 0.9989, k=32 at 0.9984) is the recorded follow-up, because one scalar cannot express two dims' floors. The 4b keeps the published 0.999 by explicit override (its E2 r3 minimum is 0.99935 full width and 0.99942 at k=32, 3.5e-4 above it) so the family's MRL floor does not loosen it; the 8b keeps its measured 0.9987 (0.99875 full width, 0.99906 at k=32). Every bound is declared with that measured evidence, never defaulted; E2's re-run measures them again.


The rc4 wave (transformers 5.20.2 on both sides) measured the served-vs-reference minimum cosine at 0.9992973389 full width and 0.9988384352 at k=32 over the same 69-vector corpus the E2 r3 wave (0.9990227618 and 0.9989077419) measured: the same vectors, so the movement is the two bf16 kernel stacks' rounding, not a cast or a library effect. The k=32 minimum is the family's binding row (row 14 query, second worst at E2 r3, moved -9.87e-5) and the corpus's largest per-vector movement at k=32 is 3.974e-4, so this size inherits the family's gates.vec_min_cosine 0.9984 = 0.9988384352 - 3.974e-4 (rounded down). It gates this variant's full width and k=1024 rows too, where the measured 0.9992973389 leaves 9.0e-4 of headroom.
